statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Current NQ structure is lower versus prior settlement but rotational within a narrow overnight range, so Tail remains below the blocking threshold while rates, oil and event risk keep Stress extreme.
recommendation: Current Tail is in the watch band. The main conditional risk window is 12:00-15:15 UTC, when U.S. data, Fed remarks and the cash-open sequence can test whether downside structure becomes persistently one-way.
headline: NQ remains lower but rotational; Tail stays in WATCH ahead of the U.S. event cluster.
body: The latest delayed December NQ quote reviewed before cutoff was 30,694.50, down 0.23% from prior settlement, inside a 30,680.25-30,713.50 session range. That two-way range and rebound from the low do not show a current no-retracement path. The U.S. 10-year yield near 5.11% and Brent around $102 keep Stress extreme.

lookbackSummary: Tail was low early September 23, rose into elevated territory during the U.S. downside phase, then de-escalated as mean reversion returned. The 05:00 UTC September 24 assessment moved back to WATCH after renewed overnight weakness.
outlookSummary: Tail remains WATCH into the European morning. The 12:00-15:15 UTC U.S. cluster is the strongest conditional risk window; blocking bands require observed persistent extension, weak retracements or session-extreme holding after the releases/open.

forecast.analysis: Delayed December NQ is 30,694.50, about 0.23% below prior settlement, inside a 30,680.25-30,713.50 session range. Rotation within that narrow band and the rebound from the low keep Tail in WATCH rather than a blocking band, while the 10-year yield near 5.11% and oil above $100 keep Stress extreme.
drivers: NQ lower versus prior settlement but rotating within the current-session range

forecast.analysis: Into the next European hour, Tail stays in WATCH if the narrow overnight rotation persists. A clean break that holds below the current range with only shallow rebounds would be the specific escalation condition.
drivers: Current overnight range as the immediate structure checkpoint

forecast.analysis: Williams speaks at 08:10 UTC. Event Stress rises, but Tail remains WATCH unless the actual market response becomes directionally efficient with failed or very shallow retracements.
drivers: John Williams moderated discussion at 08:10 UTC

forecast.analysis: After the Williams checkpoint, Tail eases within WATCH if price discovery remains two-way. Repeated extension away from the European range would keep downside-path risk elevated.
drivers: European range retention versus directional escape

forecast.analysis: Late European morning keeps Tail near the bottom of WATCH if rotations remain meaningful. A fresh extreme that persists without retracement would invalidate the de-escalation baseline.
Pre-U.S.-event positioning raises Stress and keeps Tail in WATCH. The score still assumes no persistent one-way path has been observed before the data and speaker cluster.
drivers: No pre-release assumption of directional alignment

forecast.analysis: Barkin at 12:00 UTC, jobless claims and international-transactions data at 12:30, and Hammack at 12:50 create the strongest pre-open checkpoint. Tail reaches the top of WATCH; a blocking state requires observed continuation.
drivers: Jobless claims and BEA releases at 12:30 UTC

forecast.analysis: Post-release Tail is elevated only if NQ shows sustained extension with weak retracements as the U.S. cash open approaches. Orderly two-way discovery would argue for a rapid reduction instead.
The cash-open hour and 14:00 UTC new-home-sales release form the peak conditional risk window. Tail is elevated only under persistent extension, session-extreme holding or repeated failed pullbacks.
Tail remains conditionally elevated if the opening impulse keeps extending after failed retracements. If the market rotates back through the opening range, the score should compress quickly.
By mid-morning New York, Tail falls to WATCH if the first U.S. impulse has been absorbed. Continued one-way trade with shallow pullbacks would keep the higher-risk branch active.
Late morning U.S. trade favors WATCH if directional efficiency fades. A renewed break that holds near session extremes would prevent further de-escalation.
At midday, Tail remains WATCH under a two-way tape. A fresh catalyst-driven extension without meaningful pullback would be the condition for renewed escalation.
Early afternoon risk stays in WATCH while price can retrace through prior impulses. Repeated continuation after failed retracements would keep the session from normalizing.
Tail returns to low under a normalization case in which U.S. trade becomes more rotational and cross-asset pressure stops intensifying. Renewed aligned extension would invalidate that path.
Late afternoon remains low Tail if meaningful retracements continue and NQ is no longer pinned near a session extreme. Persistent directional efficiency would be the contrary signal.
Into the final cash hour, low Tail assumes no new one-way second leg. A closing drive that repeatedly extends after weak pullbacks would raise the path-risk estimate.
After the cash close, Tail stays low if futures stabilize around a balanced post-close range. A fresh headline-driven break with no retracement would be the exception.
The first overnight hour remains low Tail if post-close liquidity is orderly and no new geopolitical or policy discontinuity appears. Thin-liquidity extension would require reassessment.
Tail stays low through the quiet overnight window if the market continues to rotate rather than trend efficiently. Persistent extension through thin liquidity would challenge that baseline.
Low Tail persists if Asia-open price discovery stays two-way. A synchronized move in NQ, yields and oil with shallow pullbacks would be the condition for a higher score.
Tail edges higher only if Asia develops a directional handoff rather than a balanced range. Otherwise the overnight structure remains compatible with mean reversion.
Approaching Europe, Tail remains low-to-mixed if overnight extremes are retraced. Holding a fresh extreme into rising European liquidity would increase persistence risk.
The next European morning starts below the blocking threshold. Tail would rise only if fresh directional extension holds with weak pullbacks and reinforcing cross-asset pressure.

forecastDetail.comment: Current NQ is lower but rotating inside a narrow range; Tail is WATCH, not blocked, while rates and oil keep Stress extreme.
WATCH persists if European trade remains rotational; a held break with shallow rebounds is the escalation test.
Williams at 08:10 UTC raises event Stress; Tail rises only if the observed response becomes persistently directional.
Post-Williams WATCH assumes orderly two-way discovery; repeated extension would keep path risk higher.
Late-European WATCH remains near the lower boundary if meaningful retracements continue.
Pre-U.S.-event WATCH reflects event proximity and high Stress, not an observed one-way path.
